diagnostics.message: local_file.public_ssh_key has an explicit depends_on = ["tls_private_key.ssh"], but its content = "${tls_private_key.ssh.public_key_openssh}" already references tls_private_key.ssh, so Terraform already infers the ordering. The depends_on is redundant.

local_file.private_ssh_key has an explicit depends_on = ["tls_private_key.ssh"], but its content = "${tls_private_key.ssh.private_key_pem}" already references tls_private_key.ssh, so Terraform already infers the ordering. The depends_on is redundant.

aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token is created with value="null" and its real value is written by the runner instance's user-data script. If the parameter does not exist yet when Terraform later applies it, it can clobber the token written during registration. The launch configuration (which defines the instance's user-data) is not ordered after aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token. Add depends_on so the parameter exists before the runner instance is created.

The runner instance configures Docker/CloudWatch logging to the log group aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment (name = var.environment), but the launch configuration does not wait for that log group to exist. If the group is absent when the agent starts logging, the awslogs driver fails. Add depends_on so the log group is created first.

The runner agent needs the docker-machine spot-request permissions from aws_iam_policy.instance_docker_machine_policy, but the role policy attachment is a sibling of the launch configuration, so the instance can boot before the policy is attached and fail to create spot requests. Order the launch configuration after aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy.

The runner agent reads/writes the GitLab registration token in SSM, requiring the permissions from aws_iam_policy.ssm. The attachment is not ordered before the instance, so registration can fail if the policy is not yet attached. Order the launch configuration after aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm.

The instance role needs the cache bucket policy (local.bucket_policy -> module.cache) attached via aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance for the agent to reach the S3 cache. This attachment is not ordered before the instance, so cache access can fail. Order the launch configuration after aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance.

The runner agent needs the service-linked-role creation permissions from aws_iam_policy.service_linked_role. This attachment is not ordered before the instance, so the agent may fail to create service-linked roles. Order the launch configuration after aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service_linked_role.

When cloudwatch logging is enabled, the inline logging permissions in aws_iam_role_policy.instance must be attached to the instance role before the runner starts, otherwise it cannot create log streams / write to CloudWatch. This inline policy is not ordered before the instance. Order the launch configuration after aws_iam_role_policy.instance.
